about.title: Calabasas Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Calabasas blends busy retail centers, hillside walkways, and shared parking structures near US-101, and any of these settings can hide a hazard that a property owner should have addressed. Wet tile near an entrance, a cracked walkway along Mulholland Highway, or a loose stair rail at an apartment complex can turn an ordinary errand into an injury. California law asks whether the property owner or manager knew, or reasonably should have known, about the dangerous condition and failed to fix or warn about it in time. That's why documenting what caused your fall matters so much, along with photos, witness names, and any surveillance footage before it's deleted. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we're a free service that puts you in touch with an independent attorney familiar with these claims. There's no cost to talk, and the attorneys in our network only get paid if your case results in a recovery. If a fall in Calabasas left you hurt, it's worth finding out where you stand before evidence disappears.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About a Calabasas Fall

items.title: Proving Notice Takes Timely Evidence
items.desc: California premises claims hinge on showing the owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An attorney can help gather incident reports, maintenance logs, and surveillance footage before a business overwrites or discards it.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you're partly responsible for the fall, you may still recover a share of damages. An attorney can help present the facts in a way that fairly accounts for your side of events.

items.title: The Clock Is Shorter Than You Might Think
items.desc: You generally have two years from the date of the fall to file a claim, and that window can be even shorter if a government-owned property was involved. Waiting too long can mean losing the right to pursue compensation altogether.

items.question: I fell at a store near the Commons at Calabasas. What should I do first?
items.answer: Report the fall to store management and ask that a written incident report be created, then take photos of the exact spot, including any spill, debris, or lighting issue. Get the names of anyone who saw it happen and ask whether the location has surveillance cameras, since that footage often gets erased on a routine schedule. Seeking medical care promptly also creates a record connecting your injuries to the fall.

items.question: Does it matter if the fall happened on a hillside path or private walkway instead of inside a business?
items.answer: No, California premises liability law applies broadly to property owners, including outdoor walkways, stairs, and common areas at apartment complexes or hillside developments common in Calabasas. The key question is still whether the owner knew or should have known about the hazardous condition and failed to address it. An attorney can evaluate the specific location and circumstances.

items.question: What if I wasn't sure whether I was partly to blame for not seeing the hazard?
items.answer: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, being partially at fault doesn't automatically bar your claim; it may just reduce the amount recovered by your percentage of responsibility. It's still worth having an independent attorney review the facts rather than assuming you have no case. Every situation is different, and small details can matter.
